title: Downtown sample screen (screen 7: the shelter street, and the guild house)
note: The level's golden screen with your 26 Oct picks 1a and 4a, built from parts, 0 credits, after two independent review rounds (all findings fixed or noted). The houses run on past the top of the screen at true scale, one window repeated on every storey, and now sit below the far layers in value (on screen: houses 145-152, old town row 169, far roofs 172-181). The guild house runs up too: its stepped gable is the portal top with a gold medallion, its chimney a slim bay window with the golden bone on its roof. Tram stop shelter (2.5 m) and a courtyard gateway (3 m, an arch in one house) behind Pepper; her perches are where they were, as bread crates, a baker's board on crate legs (mid-tone, outlined, like the apple crates). The cargo bike now rides in front of the crates, never cut at the waist. Checks: PEPPER UNCHANGED, flow 125/125, Tiled, physics 102/102, QA 0 problems, autopilot GOOD GIRL, curve T1-T4 PASS, asset QA PASS on all 11 pieces (measured as drawn, the back fade 0.28). The Downtown palette v1 is made from these pieces, so their palette check passes by construction, not as evidence.
question: Left as they are for you: the small plaza houses in front of the tall fronts (your decision 2, not picked); lamp posts across window panes (moving them moves checkpoints); the high road's stone ledges reading as shelves; the far layers and the spire hidden on the tall street (x 1180-2480); the street's hard ends (x 1180, 2480, the lone house at 2640). Screen 10 keeps the old brick gate (no house there for a gateway); the dormer's ledge reads as a lintel; the bike's depot clip at the gate. Keep the full-height street, or open gaps so the spire stays in view?
